ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=ax^{2}+bx+3$ ($a\neq 0$) intersects with the x-axis at points $A(1,0)$ and $B(-3,0)$ and with the y-axis at point $C$. Line segment $BC$ intersects with the axis of symmetry of the parabola at point $E$, with the vertex being point $D$. Find the equation of the parabola.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that the parabola $y=ax^{2}+bx+3$ passes through points $A(1,0)$ and $B(-3,0)$,\\
we have $\begin{cases} a+b+3=0 \\ 9a-3b+3=0 \end{cases}$,\\
solving these equations yields $\begin{cases} a=-1 \\ b=-2 \end{cases}$,\\
therefore, the equation of the parabola is: \boxed{y=-x^{2}-2x+3}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives coordinate axes and a downward-opening parabola. The parabola intersects the x-axis at left point B and right point A, and intersects the y-axis at point C; the dashed line indicates the axis of symmetry of the parabola, the vertex is labeled D, and segment BC intersects the axis of symmetry at E. On the right there is also an alternate figure with the same structure. Reasoning: According to the givens, the parabola is y = ax^2 + bx + 3, and it passes through A(1,0) and B(-3,0). Substituting A(1,0) gives a + b + 3 = 0. Substituting B(-3,0) gives 9a - 3b + 3 = 0. From a + b + 3 = 0, get b = -a - 3; substituting into 9a - 3b + 3 = 0 gives 9a - 3(-a - 3) + 3 = 0, namely 12a + 12 = 0, so a = -1. Then from b = -a - 3, get b = 1 - 3 = -2. Therefore the parabola equation is y = -x^2 - 2x + 3.
